question: [scripted] ECHO-03: does what the fly learned about an earlier impairment let it recognize the same impairment sooner when it returns?
hypothesis: [scripted] A self-model reset to an innate one before a remembered held-out impairment returns takes longer to conclude that it changed itself than one with its memory intact.
competing_hypothesis: [scripted] Learning an impairment from scratch is as fast as recognizing it, so memory does not shorten the time to conclude.
